The processing client transfers a copy of marked Flip topology, strips caller-supplied metadata, and the worker validates and restores its private marker.

privateWorkerBrowser.environment: development browser, explicitly marked private Float64 buffers
privateWorkerBrowser.result: Flip preserved indexed triangle winding, retained the source buffer and returned the existing Float32 output

checks: GUI and public MCP direct geometry match
coordinate bytes match retained native fixture

limitations: Experimental private Float64 restore is not enabled in production.
The private-buffer browser control calls shared operations directly; it is not a restored-project GUI/MCP comparison.
The compact component dispatcher still excludes Float64 positions. Flip output is Float32, and broader carrier precision, ownership, large-project resources and fresh native comparison remain open.
The full suite was not rerun after this change.
